collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Families who came from other islands cook their homeland dishes for a feast: hold a cooking contest, or just share.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found, growing wild in the hills, a sour orange fruit from (subject.his/her) homeland that nobody on Isola eats. (subject.He/she) wants to cook the dish of (subject.his/her) childhood for the village feast. (friend) suggests making it a contest between all the families' homeland dishes. What should the feast be?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The contest is chaos. Every dish is someone's favorite. (subject)'s sour fruit stew makes half the village pucker and the other half ask for more. The judges refuse to pick a winner, and are nearly overthrown.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Every family brings its dish and the village tries everything. (subject)'s stew is strange and wonderful. (subject) eats it with (subject.his/her) eyes closed, remembering home. Then (subject.he/she) opens them, and the village is still there.
